subject: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach

Team —

We need to kick off a short-running decision loop for our observability stack renewals (Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Sentry). Procurement has flagged that renewal windows start in mid-June, but commercial reps are already asking for our consumption numbers.

Goals for this thread:
- Align on the commercial levers we want to pursue (multi-year commit, flexible-commit, credit pools, retention-tier conversion).
- Confirm what legal needs in terms of contract redlines and data residency language.
- Decide whether to pursue a consolidated bundle (one vendor) or keep split-sourcing with retention add-ons.

I've attached a quick spend summary and our Datadog token/host usage extract (spend_summary_Q1-2027.pdf, dd_usage_Q1-2027.csv). Please review and add your top 2 recommendations by EOD Monday.

If you want, I can include the reps in a working session; prefer we have a land-and-expand negotiation playbook before we engage so we don't get boxed into a fixed, high-cost SKU.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Infrastructure Finance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: spend_summary_Q1-2027.pdf, dd_usage_Q1-2027.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach

+1 to the agenda. Quick notes after skimming the CSV:
- Datadog host counts are spiky in Q1 due to CI runners; we can likely shave 8-12% off committed host numbers if we implement ephemeral host tagging and offload CI logs to a cheaper sink.
- We have a lot of ingestion from batch analytics that could be moved to Grafana Cloud or long-term S3 archive with the retention add-on disabled for hot storage.

Recommendation (short):
1) Push for a flexible-commit (12–18 month) with quarterly true-ups rather than a strict year-commit. We get price protection but avoid over-committing at current spiky usage.
2) Ask Datadog for retention-tier credits in lieu of an immediate list-price discount — i.e., convert a portion of the rebate into lower-priced retention for 12 months to reduce token/ingest cost.

I'll prepare two charts showing spike-adjusted host/ingest forecasts and send before Monday.

-Ben
Senior SRE, Cost Optimization
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dd_usage_Q1-2027.csv
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach

Quick legal checklist:
- Please confirm whether retention tiers will change where customer PII/PII-like telemetry resides. If so, we need explicit data residency and processing clauses.
- I want a pre-approved set of redlines for: indemnity caps, data breach notification SLA (72h), and a clause for audit access limited to SOC/SaaS logs with a redacted view.
- If we're asking for credits-as-retention, contract language must specify duration, eligible datasets, and failure-remedy (credits refunded or extended).

I'll draft a contract_redlines_draft.docx and circulate. If procurement plans multi-year commits, we should add an early-exit break clause tied to material price increases (>10% Y/Y) or major SLA regressions.

-Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: contract_redlines_draft.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach

Thanks — good inputs. Proposed negotiation playbook (high level):
1) Discovery call with each vendor to validate forecast assumptions (host count, ingest, retention). Don't share full CSVs; share a normalized summary.
2) Ask for three commercial offers: a) 1-year fixed with list discounts; b) 2-year flexible commit with quarterly true-up (target 10% lower unit) + retention credits; c) 3-year heavy commit with blended credits (only if we can lock CPU/host rates).
3) Negotiate an experimental clause for a 90-day POC on retention offload for high-volume batch logs (Grafana Cloud or S3 + Loki as a cheaper sink). Vendor funds a small migration credit if performance SLAs are met.
4) Procurement asks for marketplace pricing (AWS/GCP marketplace) and any channel incentives — sometimes the same SKU is cheaper via marketplace credits.

Timing: Recommend vendor discovery next week (May 3–7), internal decision thread closes by May 14 so we have time to finalize commercial terms in May and issue signatures before mid-June.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/DD-2027-ACME-01

-Marissa
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@datadog.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability renewal: commitment structures, retention add-ons, and negotiation approach

Hi Naomi — great to be in touch.

Thanks for sharing your usage snapshot. We can absolutely put together the three commercial packages Marissa suggested. Preliminary notes:
- Flexible-commit (quarterly true-up) is doable; we'll propose a 12–24 month cadence in the quote and show modeled savings based on Ben's spike-adjusted forecast.
- Retention credits: we can convert up to 25% of the first-year rebate into retention credits for low-cost cold storage within Datadog for eligible log streams. We will need the list of eligible streams and a runbook for the POC.
- Marketplace: there's often a channel incentive if you purchase via AWS Marketplace with 1-year commit. We'll include both direct and marketplace pricing.

I'll prepare draft quotes and a DocuSign renewal worksheet for signature. If you'd like, we can set a 45-minute working session on Wed (May 5) to walk the modeling with Ben and Marissa.

Link: https://docusign.example/renewal/DD-2027-ACME-01

Best,
Miguel Torres
Enterprise Account Executive, Datadog
miguel@datadog.com
